synopsis: Recorded-data replay is an established, low-cost way to baseline the warning system and evaluate candidate perception, warning timing and braking triggers, but it cannot validate stopping because the recorded world does not react to a brake command [f94, f332, f10925, f11320, f11321]. Recording should start in October 2026 rather than wait for a prototype; the existing fleet is suitable, and a recording-and-replay pipeline could realistically be running by mid-2027 [f5168, f333, f64]. Evidence covers only the recorded sensors, mounting positions and scenarios, excludes effects upstream of the re-injection point, and ceases to represent the machine's counterfactual future at the first brake command absent from the original run [f95, f96, f108]. Reliable replay requires raw sensor inputs, synchronized timestamps, machine signals, geometry, calibration and independent ground truth; insufficient fidelity, missing metadata or large unexplained discrepancies should trigger stopping or escalation [f11899, f12991, f10928]. Camera and lidar recordings can support reconstruction and near-path novel views, but quality is restrictive—only 50 of 200 MV² sequences passed pose checks—and no validated evidence supports re-simulating an unrecorded sensor type [f3985, f3727, f3729]. Replay therefore belongs within a broader validation programme combining simulation, benches, physical tests and staged field operation, while published sources yielded no off-road OEM statement demonstrating that simulation, replay or HIL shortened validation time [f309, f257].

relations.note: Both identify independent-ground-truth raw-log replay as the established off-field warning-system baseline.
Both describe the established method for baselining the old warning system.
Both establish raw-log replay against independent ground truth as the baseline method.
Replay metrics apply only to recorded sensors, mounting positions and scenarios.
Neither replay account retests components or influences upstream of the re-injection point.
Both report no validated evidence for re-simulating unrecorded sensor types.
Recorded evidence becomes counterfactually invalid at the first previously absent brake command.
Both locate the warning-system evidence boundary at braking intervention.
Both explain why recorded history cannot establish post-intervention machine behavior.
Both report no published off-road OEM claim that these methods shortened validation.
Both identify logged-data replay as common on-road practice.
Both describe replay or re-simulation as common ADAS and ADS industry practice.
Both state that replaying logged data is common on-road practice.
Both support camera/lidar replay and novel views close to the recorded path.
Unchanging recordings explain why open-loop replay cannot show post-braking outcomes.
Starting recording before the prototype supports the proposed mid-2027 pipeline milestone.
Required data and ground truth explain escalation when fidelity or metadata are insufficient.
Low pose-check yield illustrates reconstruction and replay dependence on tracking accuracy.
